column1: # day-cp-checks.tsv — P1399. The checks the ClarityPledge sub-day reports, one row each.
# day-cp-steps.tsv beside this file says which STEPS a complete sub-day runs. This file says which
# CHECKS the founder sees and which step computes each. They are different lists because one step
# carries several checks: Wave 3 is one bash call holding lint, tests, ops issues, RLS drift,
# function grants and the privilege floor, and its single ledger row read "cp.w3 ok 0" on the
# morning RLS drift inside it exited 1 (spec §5).
# The /day renderer finds this file by name, beside the manifest the dispatcher registered. Every
# check below gets a row in the day report even if nothing printed a status for it: "not proven"
# when its step ran, "did not run" when its step did not. A check that stops reporting can never
# How a check reports: a `run` body prints `CHECK <id> <status> <detail>`, derived from an exit code
# or token the body already prints; Sentry and Mixpanel, which only the agent can see through MCP,
#   check-id    stable id; the fault keys of its findings start with its short name
#   step-id     the manifest step that computes it
#   label       what it is, in the founder's terms
#   group       the Monitoring > Systems group on the Day page
#   severity    high = its issue is Important; normal otherwise
#   connection  the service it depends on (sentry, mixpanel, beeper, gcloud) or empty
